title: Short slices matter more than the descriptor, and a learned embedding beats the hand built one on both
question: The hand built descriptor scores well inside the library and badly on real stems. Is that the weighting, the descriptor, or the query?

material.library: 9,979 indexed preview renders, 6,540 loadable, 5,870 carrying a coarse family
material.families: drums 2045, pad 835, bass 726, keys 644, lead 505, fx 257, guitar 223, mallets 200, brass 142, voice 126, strings 111, winds 56
material.stems: nine separated stems of one four minute song, WAVE 48 kHz. The two vocal stems are excluded: a sung line has no counterpart in an instrument library.

metric: Leave one out family retrieval. A probe is ranked against the index with itself removed and counts as right when the top candidate shares its coarse family. Always answering the largest family scores 0.348.

in_library_leave_one_out.note: MERT layers 3 to 8 all score between 0.604 and 0.628, so the layer choice is flat and picking one is not tuning.

stems_twenty_second_window.what_the_errors_showed: Both answered with drum kits and voice racks, whose previews are long dense musical passages. A twenty second window of a mixed performance resembles another long passage more than it resembles the instrument that plays it.

stems_one_and_a_half_second_slices.how_chosen: The MIDI export located note onsets; the four onsets per stem with the fewest other onsets inside the following 1.5 s were taken.

weight_search_rejected.why_rejected: Two points on held out data, and the winning weighting sets peakiness to 0.02 and onset rate to 0.68. That fits a library in which a third of everything is a drum, and onset rate is exactly the feature that a twenty second stem and a one shot preview disagree about for reasons other than timbre.

refusal_threshold_does_not_work.conclusion: A sung stem, which has no counterpart in the library at all, lands closer than the median real match. Distance cannot carry a refusal.

cost.mert_model: m-a-p/MERT-v1-95M, 95M parameters, 24 kHz, 5 s context, 13 layers of 768
cost.loads_without_remote_code: The published config names custom modules, but the weights load into a plain transformers HubertModel with zero missing, unexpected or mismatched keys, so no code from the hub is executed.
cost.throughput: 8.7 files per second on the Apple GPU, which is about 19 minutes for the whole library
cost.hand_built_descriptor: no dependency at all, 12.6 minutes for the whole library on ten cores

result: The query was the larger error, not the descriptor. Cutting the probe from twenty seconds to one and a half doubles the hand built descriptor's hit rate on stems, from 1 in 7 to 6 in 20.
MERT is better than the hand built descriptor on both tasks, by about 9 points inside the library and by about 10 points on slices. It is not a different order of result.
Best combination measured: MERT on short slices, 8 of 20 top 1 and 15 of 20 top 5.
Guitar fails under every combination tried, 0 of 4 top 1 in both.
Neither a better weighting nor a distance threshold helps. Both were tried and both are recorded here as negative.
scope_and_weakness: Twenty slices from five stems of one song. The per family figures rest on four probes each and cannot carry a percentage.
The best MERT layer differs by task: 4 inside the library, 9 for slice top 1, 3 and 6 for slice top 5. Choosing per task on twenty probes would be fitting to twenty probes.
The coarse families are derived from Ableton's category paths by keyword. A preset filed somewhere surprising is scored wrong through no fault of the ranking.
The slices were located with the MIDI export of this one song. Without one, onsets have to come from the audio, which is a different and unmeasured step.
One song, one genre, one generator. Nothing here says how this behaves on acoustic recordings.
